title: p-adic Hodge theory
summary: Results classed as known in the literature and missing from Mathlib, proved here with their own definitions.

modules.title: Tate's vanishing theorem, Hodge–Tate elimination and the filtration of B_dR
modules.note:
Let `χ` be the cyclotomic character `New.cyclotomicGp` of `New.Gp p = Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p)`, where the
class `[ThePrime p]` says that `p` is prime. The file also defines the filtration tⁿ B_dR⁺ of the de
Rham period field B_dR = `New.Period.BdR`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.tate_eq_zero_of_cyclotomicGp_twist`: the only `x` in `ℂ_p` with
  `χ(g) ^ u g x = χ(g) ^ v x` for all `g` near `1` is `0` when `u ≠ v`.
* `New.Period.le_of_hodgeTate_stable`: for a subspace of `ℂ_p ^ ι` stable under the Galois action
  twisted by `χ ^ u i` in the coordinate `i`, the vectors of minimal support can be taken algebraic,
  fixed and supported on one weight, by the theorems of Tate and Ax.
* `New.Period.hodgeFil`: the step tⁿ B_dR⁺, with t = `New.Period.tPeriod` a uniformiser of the
  discrete valuation ring B_dR⁺ = `New.Period.BdRPlus`, on which g acts by g t = χ(g) t
  (`New.Period.smul_tUnit_zpow`).
* `New.Period.forall_smul_eq_iff_mem_localFieldOf`: an open subgroup fixes in ℂ_p exactly its fixed
  field K in Q̄_p.
* `New.Period.BdR.exists_sub_mem_of_smul_sub_mem`: an element of B_dR that is invariant modulo a
  B_dR⁺-submodule S is congruent modulo S to an element of K; S = 0 gives the invariants of B_dR.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.OverGp`, `New.Period.localFieldOf Γ`: a homomorphism j = `toGp` from a group `Γ` to
  `New.Gp p` with open image, and the subfield of Q̄_p fixed by that image.
modules.literature:
Known result: The Ax–Sen–Tate theorem and Tate's vanishing of the invariants of C_p(i). Ax's theorem
is not proved in this file; it comes from an imported file, as `ax_mem_closure_fixedField` and
`exists_algebraic_of_fixed_near_one`, without the constant. Tate's theorem is stated for H⁰ only, on
any open subgroup, and is proved from the boundedness of the normalised trace to Q_p. A consequence
is that invariants of B_dR modulo a submodule come from the base field. Source: J. Ax, Zeros of
polynomials over local fields: the Galois action, J. Algebra 15 (1970); J. Tate, p-divisible groups
(1967), §3; proofs in Fontaine–Ouyang 3.3-3.5 and Brinon–Conrad §14.

See also `Lib.PadicHodge.Crystalline.Regularity` and `Lib.PadicHodge.PeriodRings.DeRhamPeriods`.

modules.title: W(𝔪^♭), the diagonal tensor module W(C^♭) ⊗ T and the Artin–Schreier sequence
modules.note:
`New.Period.OFlat = O^♭` is the tilt of the ring of integers of `ℂ_p`, and `New.Period.CFlat = C^♭`
is its fraction field. We write `New.Period.WittCFlat = W(C^♭)` and `A_inf = W(O^♭)`; the prime is
fixed by `[ThePrime p]`, and `New.Gp p` is the Galois group of `ℚ̄_p` over `ℚ_p`. The ideal
`W(𝔪) = W(𝔪^♭)` of `A_inf` is introduced, and the sets `W(𝔪) + p ^ m W(C^♭)` serve as neighbourhoods
of `0` for which the Galois action on `W(C^♭)` is continuous. For a group Γ (`[GroupOverGp p]`,
elements of type `GroupOverGp.G`) that maps to `Gp p`, and a representation of Γ on a ℤ_p-module T,
the module W(C^♭) ⊗ T with the diagonal action of ℤ × Γ is built, together with base change of
linear and bilinear maps. For T = ℤ_p/p^m(1) this gives an Artin–Schreier sequence: φ − 1 is onto,
and its kernel modulo W(𝔪^♭)·(1 ⊗ 1) is ℤ_p/p^m.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.wittOfMaxIdeal`: the kernel of the reduction `A_inf → W(k)`; by
  `New.Lift.mem_wittOfMaxIdeal` its elements are the Witt vectors none of whose coefficients is a
  unit.
* `New.Lift.WittCFlat.eventually_smul_sub_mem`: for `a`, `d` in `W(C^♭)` and `g` near `1` in
  `New.Gp p`, the element `(g • a - a) * d` lies in `W(𝔪) + p ^ m W(C^♭)`.
* `New.Lift.DiagTensor`: the module W(C^♭) ⊗ T with its diagonal action.
* `New.Lift.smallPart`: the A_inf-submodule W(𝔪^♭)·(1 ⊗ 1) of M = W(C^♭) ⊗ ℤ_p/p^m(1).
* `New.Lift.TateTwist.exists_eq_phi_smul_sub`,
  `New.Lift.TateTwist.exists_sub_mk_one_mem_smallPart_of_phi_smul_sub_mem` and
  `New.Lift.TateTwist.eq_zero_of_mk_one_mem_smallPart`: φ − 1 is onto M, and its kernel modulo
  W(𝔪^♭)·(1 ⊗ 1) is ℤ_p/p^m.
* `New.Lift.TateTwist.eventually_map_smul_sub_mem_smallPart`: let ρ be a representation with
  ρ(g)y − y divisible by p^m for g near 1, and let L be a linear map from W(C^♭) ⊗ ρ into M. Then
  for each v, L(gv − v) lies in W(𝔪^♭)·(1 ⊗ 1) for g near 1.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.toWittResidue`: the ring map `A_inf = W(O^♭) → W(k)`, `k` the residue field of `O^♭`,
  that reduces each Witt coordinate.
* `New.Lift.FrobGroup Γ`: the group `ℤ × Γ`; `FrobGroup.snd` is the projection to `Γ`, `inr g` is
  `(0, g)` and `φ` is `(1, 1)`, which acts as the Frobenius.
* `New.Period.nearOne Γ`: the filter "near `1`" on `Γ`, pulled back from the neighbourhoods of `1`
  in `Gp p`.
modules.literature:
Known result: The Artin–Schreier–Witt resolution over the tilt. Only the φ−1 step of Herr's complex
is treated, on Witt vectors of the tilt of C_p modulo p^m, and the Γ-step is not treated. Source: L.
Herr, Sur la cohomologie galoisienne des corps p-adiques, Bull. SMF 126 (1998) 563–600.

modules.title: Bloch–Kato crystalline cocycles: reduction modulo p^m, rank and vanishing
modules.note:
Let `T` be a finite free `ℤ_[p]`-module of rank d with an action `ρ` of a group Γ, and let
j = `𝒥.toGp`, given by the structure `𝒥 : New.Period.OverGp Γ p`, map Γ with open image of index n
to the absolute Galois group `New.Gp` of ℚ_p. The Bloch–Kato cocycles
Z_f(T) = `New.Period.crysCocycles ρ` are the maps Γ → T that become coboundaries over the period
ring B = `New.Period.Bmax`. χ = `New.Period.χ` is the cyclotomic character `New.cyclotomicGp`
composed with j. The file proves basic properties of Z_f(T), builds admissible extensions from
crystalline cocycles of potentially crystalline representations, studies reduction modulo p^m, and
computes the rank of Z_f(T) and its vanishing.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline.exists_hodge_basis`: for potentially crystalline T, in a
  ℤ_p-basis of T, an automorphism of B_dR^ι that makes the action of Γ coordinatewise and carries
  (B_dR^+)^ι to the lattice given by the jumps of T.
* `New.Period.extensionRep`, `New.Period.isAdmissible_extensionRep`: the extension of a trivial
  module by T given by cocycles in `New.Period.crysCocycles` is admissible along the same filter as
  T (`New.Period.IsAdmissible`).
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline.reducedCocycle`: for an equivariant additive map `q` from `T`
  to a discrete module `V` with kernel `p ^ m T`, the map sending a crystalline cocycle `c` to the
  continuous cocycle `q ∘ c`.
* `New.Period.crysCocycles.finrank_eq`: for potentially crystalline T, Z_f(T) is finitely generated
  over ℤ_p of rank d + n·(number of negative Hodge–Tate jumps).
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline.exists_coboundary_eq_smul`: for potentially crystalline T
  with positive jumps, Z_f(T) is torsion modulo coboundaries.
* `New.Period.crysCocycles.apply_eq_zero_of_cyclotomicGp`: let Γ act through χ^(−a) with a ≥ 0. Then
  crystalline cocycles vanish where the action is trivial. When a = 0 we also need j(s) to lie in
  inertia.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline`: the elements of Bmax ⊗ T fixed by all g with j(g) near 1
  span Bmax ⊗ T over Bmax.
* `New.DiscreteModule`: A discrete Γ-module over R: an R-module with the discrete topology and a
  continuous R-linear action of the topological group Γ.
* `New.DiscreteModule.HoldsCorestrictions`: for a discrete Γ-module V, an open subgroup U of Γ and
  groups of cocycles Y′ ≤ Z¹(U, V) and Y ≤ Z¹(Γ, V), the group Y contains every coboundary and a
  corestriction of each y in Y′: there is a cocycle F with values in the functions Γ/U → V whose
  Shapiro image is y and whose sum over Γ/U lies in Y.
* `New.Period.jump`: The multiplicity of the Hodge–Tate jump u at γ: the dimension over Q̄_p (zero
  if infinite) of the γ-semilinear f : T → ℂ_p with f(gx) = χ(g)^(−u)·g f(x) for g near 1.
modules.literature:
Known result: Bloch–Kato finite local condition, rank formula. Here it is treated on cocycles of a
lattice in a potentially crystalline representation. The rank is counted from the fundamental exact
sequence. Local duality is not treated in this file, only the reduction of crystalline cocycles
modulo p^m. Source: S. Bloch, K. Kato, L-functions and Tamagawa numbers of motives, Grothendieck
Festschrift I (1990), Prop. 3.8, Cor. 3.8.4; J. Bellaïche, An introduction to the conjecture of
Bloch and Kato, Clay Summer School notes (2009), Prop. 2.8, Thm 2.1.

modules.title: The radius lemma: after Frobenius a frame is a constant basis times a unit over A
modules.note:
The radius lemma for a chart (`New.Lift.Chart`): a subring S of A_inf, the image of Λ⟦X⟧, where
Λ = W(𝔽_{p^𝔣}) are the constants; the image z of X is a Teichmüller lift, and E = z^e·(unit) + p is
an associate of ξ. Further A = `New.Period.Amax`, B⁺ = A[1/p] = `New.Period.BPlus`, φ is the
Frobenius, and t is a Galois element with `c.FixesThetaZ t`.

* `New.Lift.Chart.exists_E_pow_mul_eq_tau_pow_mul_iff`: A_inf[1/τ] ∩ S_B[1/E] = S.
* `New.Lift.Chart.tau_mul_z_dvd_smul_sub`: τz divides ty − y in B⁺ for every y in S_B.
* `New.Lift.Chart.radius_lemma`: if tz = [ε]z, Z has entries in S_B with Z'·Z = E^h and tZ = Z·G for
  some G over A_inf, and 3e ≤ p^l, then φ^l(Z) = φ^l(E)^b·C·V with C constant and V invertible over
  A (`New.Lift.Chart.IsRadiusFactorization`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.tau`, `New.Period.mu`, `New.Period.xi`: the elements τ = [ε^{1/p}] − 1, μ = [ε] − 1
  and ξ of A_inf, with ξτ = μ; `New.Period.theta` is Fontaine's map θ : A_inf → O_C.
* `New.Lift.Chart.ainfToBPlus`: the structure ring homomorphism from A_inf to B⁺.
* `New.Lift.Chart.bicommutant`: the S-subalgebra S_B of the y in B⁺ whose multiplication commutes
  with every S-linear endomorphism of B⁺ that preserves the image of A. It contains p⁻¹ and is the
  p-adic closure of S[E/p] with p inverted (`New.Lift.Chart.adjoinEDivPClosure_eq_bicommutant`).
* `New.Lift.Chart.FixesThetaZ`: `c.FixesThetaZ t` says that t fixes the constants Λ and θ(z).
modules.literature:
Known result: Dwork's trick, giving an integral crystalline comparison with a uniform denominator.
Here `radius_lemma` gives φ^l(Z) = φ^l(E)^b·C·V, with C fixed by every g that fixes Λ and V
invertible over A_max. Whenever e·A ≤ p^l·δ, the y with Vy natural modulo E^A span at least
p^{4δ}S^d.
Source: M. Kisin, Crystalline representations and F-crystals, Progr. Math. 253 (2006), Lemma 1.2.6;
M. Kisin, Potentially semi-stable deformation rings, JAMS 21 (2008), Lemma 2.2; B. Bhatt,
P. Scholze, Prismatic F-crystals and crystalline Galois representations (2023), proof of Thm 5.6.

See also `Lib.PadicHodge.Kisin.PeriodMatrixFrame`.

modules.title: p-adic avatars of Hecke characters and local conditions for twists and characters
modules.note:
The file constructs the `p`-adic avatar of an algebraic Hecke character of a totally complex field
`K`. This is a continuous character of the absolute Galois group `Γ`, defined after fixing
`ι : ℂ ≃ ℚ̄_p`. The file then studies local conditions on a Galois representation `r` at a place `A`
of `Ω`: finite type, good, Hodge–Tate jumps, and polynomials killing an element.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.AlgHeckeChar.avatar`: the continuous character of `Γ` obtained from an algebraic Hecke
  character `(θ, n)` by correcting `ι ∘ θ` at the places above `p`. It is multiplicative in
  `(θ, n)`.
* `New.GaloisRep.localConditions_twist`: how the local conditions `New.GaloisRep.IsFiniteTypeAt`
  (finite type), `New.GaloisRep.IsGoodAt` (unramified, or crystalline above `ℓ`),
  `New.GaloisRep.JumpsRelAt` (Hodge–Tate jumps) and `New.GaloisRep.PolyKillsAt` (a polynomial kills
  an element) behave when a representation is multiplied by a character. It collects the four
  lemmas `IsFiniteTypeAt.twist`, `IsGoodAt.twist`, `JumpsRelAt.twist` and `PolyKillsAt.twist`.
* `New.Period.isPotentiallyCrystalline_of_unramified_char`: take a continuous `p`-adic character `ν`
  of an open subgroup of `G_p`, trivial on inertia near `1`. An algebra on which `ν` acts by scalars
  is potentially crystalline (`IsPotentiallyCrystalline.of_unramified_char`) with the jumps of the
  trivial action (`jump_eq_jump_one_of_unramified_char`). Weil elements act on its Weil–Deligne
  representation through `ν` (`isKilledBy_X_sub_C_of_unramified_char`).
* `New.GaloisRep.localConditions_char_of_finite_image_inertia`: the conditions for a character with
  finite image on inertia, collected from `IsFiniteTypeAt.scalar_of_finite_image_inertia`,
  `hasJumpsAt_zero_of_finite_image_inertia` and `polyKillsAt_X_sub_C_of_finite_image_inertia`.
* `New.GaloisRep.AvatarCompatAt`: local-global compatibility for the ℓ-adic avatar
  `New.AlgHeckeChar.avatar` of an algebraic Hecke character θ of a totally complex field E;
  `New.GaloisRep.AvatarCompatAt.isSphericalAbove_of_unramified` is its consequence where θ is
  unramified.
* `New.GaloisRep.avatarCompatAt_of_type_eq_zero`: it holds at a place w of E if the infinity type
  vanishes at the embeddings over w.

Notions from other files:
* `New.AlgHeckeChar`: The type of algebraic Hecke characters of K: pairs (θ, n) of a character of
  the finite ideles and its infinity type, as in `New.algHeckeChars`.
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline`: the elements of `Bmax ⊗ T` fixed by all `g` near `1`
  (`New.Period.Dpcris`) span `Bmax ⊗ T` over `Bmax`.
* `New.GaloisRep.HasJumpsAt`: For each local datum at `A` with embedding `e`, each `g` in
  `Gal(ℚ̄_ℓ/ℚ_ℓ)` and the embedding `γ` of `ℚ̄_ℓ` in `ℂ_ℓ` given by `g`, the Hodge–Tate jumps of
  `r` at `γ`, with multiplicity, are `J` at the embedding `ι_ℓ⁻¹ ∘ g⁻¹ ∘ e` of `E` in `ℂ`.
* `New.Period.IsKilledBy`: `T` is potentially crystalline and the polynomial `P` kills
  `New.Period.linearFrob ρ s k`, the `Bmax`-linear extension of `φ ^ k s ⊗ ρ s` from `Dpcris`.
* `New.IsFrob`: `σ` stabilises the valuation subring `A` and `σ • x ≡ x ^ q` modulo the maximal
  ideal for all `x ∈ A`.
modules.literature:
Known result: Characters with finite image on inertia are potentially crystalline of weight 0. Only
the potentially unramified case of the theorem on locally algebraic characters is covered, together
with the jumps and the action of Weil elements. The period is a solution of Lang's equation for GL_1
in A_inf with coefficients, and no Lubin–Tate theory is used. Source: B. Conrad, Lifting global
representations with local properties (preprint 2011), Appendix B; J.-P. Serre, Abelian l-adic
representations (1968), III, Appendix.

See also `Lib.ClassField.Avatar.LocalGlobalCompatibility` and
`Lib.PadicHodge.Crystalline.Regularity`.

modules.title: Crystalline and potentially crystalline representations and admissibility
modules.note:
This file concerns a representation `ρ` of a group `Γ` on an `R`-module `T`. The group `Γ` carries a
homomorphism `j` (the field `toGp` of `New.Period.OverGp`) with open image in the Galois group
`New.Gp p` of `ℚ_[p]`. Tensor products are over `ℤ_[p]` and the period ring is `New.Period.Bmax`;
the class `ThePrime p` makes `p` a prime (it supplies the `Fact p.Prime` needed by `OverGp`).

"Near `1`" means along the filter `New.Period.nearOne`, which takes the place of passing to a finite
extension. Let `B` be a `ℤ_[p]`-algebra with an action of `New.Gp p`. The diagonal action
`New.Period.tensorAction` of `g` on `B ⊗ T` is `j(g) ⊗ ρ(g)`. For a filter `F` on `Γ`,
`New.Period.fixedPeriods ρ B F` is the set of elements of `B ⊗ T` fixed by the diagonal action for
`F`-almost all `g`. `New.Period.IsAdmissible ρ F` says that for `B = Bmax` this set spans `B ⊗ T`
over `B`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.IsCrystalline`, `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline`: the vectors of `Bmax ⊗ T` fixed
  by `Γ`, or fixed near `1` (`New.Period.Dpcris`), span `Bmax ⊗ T`.
* `New.Period.crysCocycles`: the functions `Γ → T` that become coboundaries in `Bmax ⊗ T`.
* `New.Period.hodgeTateMaps`, `New.Period.HasJumps`: Hodge–Tate maps `T → ℂ_[p]` of weight `u` along
  `γ : R → ℂ_[p]`, and the multiset of weights counted with the dimensions of these spaces.
* `New.Period.IsWeilPair`, `New.Period.linearFrob`, `New.Period.IsKilledBy`: the action of `φ ^ m s`
  on `Dpcris`, extended linearly, and the polynomials over `R` that annihilate it.
* `New.Period.IsAdmissible.tate_twist`, `New.Period.isAdmissible_of_cyclotomicGp_zpow`: twists by
  powers of the cyclotomic character, through the unit of `New.Period.exists_tate_twist_unit`.
* `New.Period.equivFun_tensorAction`: in the coordinates given by a finite basis `e` of `T`, the
  diagonal action is `New.Period.coordAction`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.Bmax`: the period ring B⁺[1/μ] (Colmez's B_max), used here in place of B_cris.
* `New.Period.FrobGal`: the monoid ℕ × `Gp p`; on the period rings with a Frobenius `φ`, the pair
  `(n, g)` acts as `φ ^ n ∘ g`.

modules.title: Semilinear forms of given weight: independence, finiteness, and jumps read off a basis
modules.note:
`New.Period.hodgeTateMaps ρ γ u` is the `PadicAlgCl p`-space of `γ`-semilinear maps `f : T → ℂ_[p]`
with `f (ρ g x) = χ(g) ^ (-u) • toGp g • f x` for `g` near `1`. Here `toGp` is the map to `Gp p`
given by the instance `[OverGp Γ p]`, and the instance `[ThePrime p]` fixes `p` as a prime. For
`toGp` of open image and `T` finite over `R`:
* `New.Period.hodgeTateMaps.mem_span_same_weight`: a map of weight `u` in the `ℂ_[p]`-span of maps
  `f i` of weights `k i` lies in the `PadicAlgCl p`-span of those with `k i = u`;
* `New.Period.finite_hodgeTateMaps`: each space has finite dimension;
* `New.Period.hasJumps_of_basis`: the weights of a `ℂ_[p]`-basis of such maps are the jumps
  (`New.Period.HasJumps`).

The input is that an element of `ℂ_[p]` fixed near `1` is algebraic, and is zero if it is fixed
after twisting by a nonzero power of `χ`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.nearOne`: The filter 'near 1' on Γ: the pull-back along `toGp : Γ → G_p` of the filter
  of neighbourhoods of the identity.
* `New.cyclotomicGp`: The p-adic cyclotomic character χ of G_p = Gal(Q̄_p over Q_p) (`New.Gp`); for
  `g : Γ`, `χ g` means χ applied to `toGp g`.
* `New.Period.jump`, `New.Period.HasJumps`: the multiplicity of the jump u is the dimension over
  `PadicAlgCl p` of `hodgeTateMaps ρ γ u`; a multiset J of integers gives the jumps if each u occurs
  in J with that multiplicity.

modules.title: Hodge frames and Hodge–Tate jumps under operations on representations
modules.note:
This file works with the period ring B_dR⁺, its uniformiser `t` and its residue map θ to ℂ_p. An
invertible matrix `U` of de Rham periods with `N g · g U = U` for `g` near 1 is brought into the
form `New.Period.hodgeMatrix W k` by an algebraic change of basis, and the columns of θ(W) are then
Hodge–Tate vectors. From this the file builds Hodge–Tate frames of potentially crystalline
representations, counts their jumps, and computes the jumps under base change, restriction of
scalars, twists, duals and submodules of products.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.exists_isHodgeFrame`: an invertible `U` over B_dR with `N g · g U = U` becomes
  `hodgeMatrix W k`, with `W` invertible over B_dR⁺, after an algebraic change of basis of
  determinant 1.
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline.exists_isHodgeTateFrame`: there is an invertible `P` over
  `ℂ_[p]` whose columns are Hodge–Tate vectors of weights `k` (`New.Period.IsHodgeTateFrame`); the
  `k i` are the jumps, and the rows of `P⁻¹` form a basis of Hodge–Tate maps
  (`New.Period.hodgeTateMaps`).
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline.exists_hasJumps`: the number of jumps is the rank.
* `New.Period.jump_baseChange`, `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline.sum_jump_eq_jump_overZp`:
  extension, restriction of scalars.
* `New.Period.jump_twist_of_period`, `New.Period.jump_twist_cyclotomicGp`,
  `New.Period.hasJumps_of_cyclotomicGp_zpow`: twists shift jumps.
* `New.Period.exists_jump_of_jointly_injective`: a jump of a submodule of ∏ S_i is a jump of some
  S_i.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.BdRPlus`, `New.Period.BdR` (built for the prime p fixed by the instance `ThePrime p`,
  hence written without `p`): the discrete valuation ring B_dR⁺, with uniformiser `t`
  (`New.Period.tPeriod`) and residue map θ to ℂ_p (`New.Period.thetaBdR`), and its fraction field
  B_dR.
* `New.cyclotomicGp`: The p-adic cyclotomic character χ of G_p = Gal(Q̄_p over Q_p) (`New.Gp`);
  `New.Period.χ` is its composite with `toGp : Γ → G_p`, the map supplied by the class `OverGp Γ p`;
  the "open image" of `toGp` assumed in the lemmas comes with this class.
* `New.Period.nearOne`: The filter 'near 1' on Γ: the pull-back along `toGp` of the filter of
  neighbourhoods of the identity.
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline`: ρ is potentially crystalline: the vectors of Bmax ⊗ T (Bmax
  the crystalline period ring B_max, a ℤ_p-algebra on which G_p acts) fixed by `toGp g ⊗ ρ g` for
  `g` near 1 span Bmax ⊗ T.
* `New.Period.hodgeTateMaps`, `New.Period.jump`: the space of γ-semilinear forms f on T with f(g
  x) = χ(g)^(−u) · g f(x) for g near 1, and its dimension, the multiplicity of the jump u.
* `New.Period.overZp`: A representation of Γ on a module T over a Z_p-algebra R, regarded as a
  Z_p-linear representation.
* `New.Period.HasJumps`: The property of a multiset J of integers that for every integer u the
  multiplicity of the jump u of T at γ equals its count in J.

modules.title: Bounded poles, φ-fixed elements of B_max, and ratios of periods fixed near 1
modules.note:
The period ring `B = B⁺[1/μ]` (`New.Period.Bmax`, `New.Period.BPlus`) lies inside `B_dR`, and `φ`
denotes its Frobenius. This file shows that bounded poles of the `φ^n y` control the denominators
of `y` in `μ`, and that a `φ`-fixed element of `B` lying in `B_dR⁺` is in `ℚ_[p]`. Using charts
(`New.Lift.Chart`), it shows that a ratio of two periods that is fixed by an open subgroup of `G_p`
lies in `W(𝔽_q)[1/p]` for some `q`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.pow_smul_mem_range_BPlus`: if the image of `φ^n(y)` in `B_dR` lies in
  `t^(−a)B_dR⁺` for every `n ≥ 0`, then `ν^a y` lies in the image of `B⁺` for every `ν` in `A_inf`
  divisible by `μ`.
* `New.Period.Bmax.exists_padic_eq_of_frobEnd_fixed`: kernel in the fundamental exact sequence: an
  element `y` of `B` with `φ(y) = y` whose image in `B_dR` lies in `B_dR⁺` belongs to `ℚ_[p]`.
* `New.Period.exists_pow_mul_eq_wittFq_mul_of_isChartOf`, `New.Period.Bmax.exists_witt_ratio`: a
  ratio of two periods that is fixed by an open subgroup of `G_p` lies in `W(𝔽_q)[1/p]` for some
  `q`, for a given chart and in general.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.BdRPlus`: the ξ-adic completion of B⁺, with fraction field `New.Period.BdR`.
* `New.Period.BPlus`, `New.Period.Bmax`: B⁺ = A_max[1/p] and B = B⁺[1/μ], μ = [ε] − 1.
* `New.Lift.Chart.bicommutant`: the S-algebra S_B of the y in B⁺ whose multiplication commutes with
  every S-linear endomorphism of B⁺ that keeps the image of A_max.

modules.title: Regularity of B_max, closure of admissibility, and crystalline descent from inertia
modules.note:
This file proves the regularity of the period ring `B = New.Period.Bmax` and shows that
representations admissible along a filter have bases of fixed elements. It proves closure
properties of crystalline and potentially crystalline representations under subobjects, quotients
of tensor products and twisted duals. It also shows that a potentially crystalline representation
is crystalline when the linear Frobenius operators are trivial on inertia.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.fontaine_regularity`, `New.Period.IsAdmissible.exists_basis`: regularity of `B`; bases
  of fixed elements.
* `New.Period.IsAdmissible.of_jointly_injective`, `New.Period.IsKilledBy.of_jointly_injective`:
  subobjects of finite sums.
* `New.Period.linearFrob_apply`, `New.Period.linearFrob_mul`,
  `New.Period.linearFrob_twist_cyclotomicGp`,
  `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline.eventually_linearFrob_eq_one`: the operators are
  multiplicative and change by a power of `p` under Tate twists. They are trivial on inertia near
  `1` if `T` is finite free.
* `New.Period.IsAdmissible.of_bilinear`, `New.Period.linearFrob_baseChangePairing`: quotients of
  tensor products.
* `New.Period.IsAdmissible.of_pairing`: twisted duals.
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline.isCrystalline_of_inertia_fixes`: descent from inertia.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.BPlus`, `New.Period.Bmax`: B⁺ = A_max[1/p] and B = B⁺[1/μ], μ = [ε] − 1.
* `New.Period.nearOne`: The filter 'near 1' on Γ: the pull-back along j: Γ → G_p of the filter of
  neighbourhoods of the identity.
* `New.Period.IsWeilPair`: (s, m) is a Weil pair if s acts on the residue field of the integers of
  Q̄_p as x ↦ x^(1/p^m); m = 0 means that s is in inertia.
modules.literature:
Known result: Potentially crystalline representations, Hodge–Tate weights and Weil–Deligne
Frobenius. Here the representations are abstract modules over any p-adic coefficient ring, with
Colmez's B_max as period ring and "crystalline" defined by the invariants spanning. Polynomials
killing one linear Frobenius replace the Weil–Deligne representation. Source: J.-M. Fontaine,
Représentations p-adiques semi-stables (Exp. III §1, §5) and Représentations l-adiques
potentiellement semi-stables (Exp. VIII 2.3), Astérisque 223 (1994); O. Brinon, B. Conrad, CMI
Summer School notes on p-adic Hodge theory (2009), 2.3.1, 5.2.1, 6.3, 9.1–9.3.

See also `Lib.PadicHodge.PeriodRings.DeRhamPeriods` and `Lib.PadicHodge.Kisin.PeriodMatrixFrame`.

modules.title: Power series charts Λ⟦z⟧ in A_inf: Weierstrass division and fixed elements
modules.group: Charts, period matrices and Kisin modules
modules.note:
A chart `c` presents a power series ring `S = Λ⟦z⟧` inside `New.Period.Ainf` (A_inf), the Witt
vectors of the tilt `New.Period.OFlat` of the integers of `ℂ_p`. Here `Λ` is the ring of Witt
vectors of the field with `p ^ f` elements, and `z = [ϖ^♭]` is the Teichmüller lift of the chart's
element `ϖ^♭ = c.varpiFlat` of the tilt (`c.seriesMap_X`). The chart sends `X ^ e * A + p`, where
`A` is the unit series `c.unitSeries`, to a generator `E` of the kernel of Fontaine's map `θ`
(`New.Period.theta`). ξ = `New.Period.xi` also generates the kernel of `θ`. `New.Gp p` = G_p, the
absolute Galois group of `ℚ_p`, acts on A_inf; the class `ThePrime p` fixes the prime `p`
throughout. The maps `θ ∘ φ^{-n}` show that elements of the tilt fixed by the Galois elements fixing
`S` are approximated from `S`. `S`-linear maps of A_inf extend to B^+ = `BPlus` = A_max[1/p], where
A_max = `Amax` has image `amaxImage` in B^+.

This file constructs charts and their ring `S`, and gives A_inf a topological basis over `S`. It
proves that Frobenius preserves `S` and proves Weierstrass division by `φ^n E`. It studies the maps
`θ ∘ φ^{-n}` and proves the approximation theorem for fixed elements of the tilt. The extension of
`S`-linear maps to B^+ is treated in `Lib.PadicHodge.Kisin.Bicommutant`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.Chart.φ`: Frobenius preserves `S`. `New.Lift.Chart.weierstrass_division`: division by
  `φ^n E`.
* `New.Lift.thetaPhiInv`: the map `θ ∘ φ^{-n}` to the integers of `ℂ_p`. Modulo `p` it is the `n`-th
  component of the reduction modulo `p` (`New.Lift.mk_thetaPhiInv_eq_coeff`), and its kernel is
  generated by `φ^n E` (`New.Lift.frobE_dvd_iff`).
* `New.Lift.Chart.eventually_exists_coeff_eq_of_fixed`: the approximation theorem, from Ax's theorem
  (`New.Period.ax_mem_closure_fixedField`) and `New.Lift.Chart.mem_of_fixed_thetaPhiInvS`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.AdicBasis`: A topological basis of `M` over `S` for the `I`-adic topology: vectors `b i`
  whose finite combinations are dense, with linear forms `coord i` on `M` that read off the
  coefficients of a finite combination.
* `New.Period.FrobGal`: The monoid ℕ × G_p; the pair (n, g) acts on A_inf as φ^n g.

modules.title: The ring S_B of a chart and extension of S-linear maps of A_inf to B^+
modules.group: Charts, period matrices and Kisin modules
modules.note:
This file works in B^+ = `BPlus` = A_max[1/p], where A_max = `Amax` has image `amaxImage` in B^+.
It defines the ring S_B of a chart, the elements of B^+ whose multiplication commutes with all
`S`-linear maps of B^+ that keep `amaxImage`. It shows that S_B is the closure of `S[E/p]` with `p`
inverted, and that every `S`-linear map of A_inf extends to an S_B-linear map of B^+ that keeps
`amaxImage`. Most identities for the extensions are checked on A_inf by a density principle: an
additive map of B^+ that keeps `amaxImage` and kills A_inf is zero
(`New.Lift.Chart.eq_zero_of_map_ainfToBPlus_eq_zero`). The file ends with results on divisibility
by `z` in B^+.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.Chart.bicommutant`: the ring S_B of the elements of B^+ whose multiplication commutes
  with all S-linear maps B^+ → B^+ that keep the image of A_max.
* `New.Lift.Chart.extendToBPlus`: an S-linear map of A_inf extends to an S_B-linear map of B^+
  keeping the image of A_max.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.Amax`: Colmez's period ring A_max, the p-adic completion of A_inf[X]/(pX − ξ).
* `New.Period.FrobGal`: The monoid ℕ × G_p; the pair (n, g) acts on A_inf as φ^n g.
* `New.Lift.Chart.S`: the ring `S`, the image in A_inf of the chart's map Λ[[X]] → A_inf.
* `New.Lift.Chart.E`: the image `E` in `S` of the series X^e A + p; it equals ξ times a unit.
* `New.Lift.Chart.adicBasis`: a chosen (p, z)-adic topological basis of A_inf over `S`, whose
  coordinate at `New.Lift.Chart.oneIndex` is the identity on `S`.

modules.title: Witt coefficients, the Frobenius group action and existence of Kummer charts
modules.group: Charts, period matrices and Kisin modules
modules.note:
Let Λ = `New.Lift.WittFq f` be the ring of Witt vectors of the field with p^f elements inside O^♭,
with p implicit, and let θ be Fontaine's map from A_inf to O_C. The group ℤ × Γ acts on O^♭, A_inf
and W(C^♭), where (n, g) acts as φ^n j(g) and φ is the bijective Frobenius. A local field is given
by `Γ : GroupOverGp p`, a group with a homomorphism j = `toGp` to `Gp p` of open image; the field is
the subfield of ℚ̄_p fixed by the image. Every such field has a Kummer chart: a chart
S = Λ⟦z⟧ ⊂ A_inf with a subgroup Γ' of Γ of index prime to p, such that j(Γ') fixes Λ and θ(z) and
moves z to every [ε]^l z.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.wittToQpBar`: the restriction of θ to Λ, with values in the algebraic closure of
  `ℚ_[p]`; it is injective (`New.Lift.wittToQpBar_injective`).
* `New.Lift.FrobGroup`: the group ℤ × Γ, with Frobenius `New.Lift.FrobGroup.φ`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart`: a Kummer chart; `New.Lift.KummerChart.IsUnramified`: it is unramified.
* `New.Lift.exists_kummerChart`: every such field has a Kummer chart, with ef the degree of the
  field.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.OFlat`: The ring O^♭, the inverse limit of O_C/p along x ↦ x^p, where O_C is the ring
  of integers of C_p.
* `New.Lift.Chart`: A Λ-algebra map Λ[[X]] → A_inf with image S, sending X to a non-unit Teichmüller
  lift z and a series X^e A + p, A a unit, to an element E that generates ker θ.

modules.title: Period matrices over a chart: lattice bases and existence for crystalline lattices
modules.group: Charts, period matrices and Kisin modules
modules.note:
This file studies period matrices over a chart `c` (`New.Lift.Chart`). `A_inf ⊂ B⁺ = A_max[1/p]` are
the period rings `New.Period.Ainf`, `New.Period.BPlus`, and `amaxImage` is the image of `A_max` in
`B⁺`. A chart gives a subring `S` of `A_inf` with elements `z` and `E`. Here `E` is `ξ` times a
unit, and `ξ` generates the kernel of `θ`. `S_B` denotes `New.Lift.Chart.bicommutant`. Write
`μ = [ε] - 1` (`New.Period.mu`) and `τ = [ε^{1/p}] - 1` (`New.Period.tau`). Then `E τ` is `μ` times
a unit.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.Chart.IsPeriodMatrix`: period matrices `U` over `B⁺` of height `h`.
* `New.Lift.Chart.IsPeriodMatrix.exists_basis`: a basis `Q`, `Z` for `U`
  (`New.Lift.Chart.IsPeriodBasis`): the `x` over `A_inf` with `E ^ h x ∈ U S_B ^ d` are the `S`-span
  of the columns of a nonsingular matrix `Q`.
* `New.Lift.Chart.IsChartOf.exists_mem_bicommutant_of_fixed`: elements of `New.Period.Bmax` fixed by
  `Γ` come from `c.bicommutant`, an `S`-subalgebra of `New.Period.BPlus` in which `p` is invertible
  (defined as a commutant, `New.Lift.Chart.bicommutant`).
* `New.Lift.Chart.IsChartOf.exists_isPeriodMatrixOf`: if the Hodge–Tate jumps lie in `[-a, b]`, an
  invariant basis `M` gives the period matrix `(E τ) ^ a M` of height `a + b`
  (`New.Lift.Chart.IsPeriodMatrix`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.mu`, `New.Period.tau`, `New.Period.xi`: The elements μ = [ε] − 1, τ = [ε^{1/p}] − 1
  and ξ = ∑_{i<p} [ε^{1/p}]^i of A_inf, with ξτ = μ; brackets denote Teichmüller lifts, and ε = (1,
  ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …) is `New.Period.epsTilt`.
* `New.Lift.Chart.z`, `New.Lift.Chart.E`: For a chart, the images in S of X and of the series X^e
  A + p, A a unit of Λ[[X]]. Here Λ = `New.Lift.WittFq` = W(F_{p^f}).
* `New.Period.jump`: The multiplicity of an integer as a Hodge–Tate jump of ρ at an embedding.
* `New.Lift.Chart.IsChartOf`: The field of the chart contains the field fixed by the image of j:
  Γ → G_p: every g in G_p that fixes Λ pointwise and fixes θ(z) lies in the image of j.
* `New.Lift.Chart.extendToBPlus`: a chosen `S`-linear extension to `B⁺` of an `S`-linear map
  `A_inf → A_inf`; it maps `amaxImage` into itself.
* `New.Period.frobEnd`: the Frobenius endomorphism `φ` of the period rings.

modules.title: Kummer charts: the different, the primes φ^a E of A_inf and their images in B_dR
modules.group: Charts, period matrices and Kisin modules
modules.note:
Fix a Kummer chart `k` (`New.Lift.KummerChart`) with ring `S ⊆ A_inf` and distinguished element `E`.
The file studies the elements p_a = φ^a E and δ = zτ of A_inf and bounds the different of the chart.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.exists_derivative_dvd_p_pow`: a bound for the different.
* `New.Lift.phiInvToBdR`: the map `r ↦ φ^{-a} r` from `A_inf` to `B_dR`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.phiInvToBdR_mem_hodgeFil_one_iff`,
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.phiInvToBdR_frobE_zpow_mem_hodgeFil`: it sends `r` to an element of positive
  order exactly when `φ^a E` divides `r`, and the `m`-th power of the image of `φ^a E` has order at
  least `m`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.valueField`: the subfield `𝒦_a` of `B_dR` in which values are taken.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.sum_phiInvToBdR_map_mul_mem_of_mem_valueField`: `S`-linear maps `A_inf → S`
  preserve linear relations over `𝒦_a`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.smul_sub_mem_hodgeFil_of_valueField`: if `φ^a E` divides `gs − s` for all
  `s` in `S`, then `g` fixes the elements of `𝒦_a` of order at least `0` modulo `t`; more generally,
  the same holds for the sums `∑ l, t l s` and `∑ l, t l x`, with the `t l` in the Galois monoid.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.Ainf`: the ring A_inf of p-typical Witt vectors over the tilt O^♭ of the ring O_C of
  integers of C_p.
* `New.Period.tau`, `New.Period.xi`: τ = [ε^(1/p)] − 1, with φ τ = μ = [ε] − 1, and ξ = μ/τ.
* `New.Lift.FrobGroup`: the group ℤ × Γ, acting on A_inf by (n, g) ↦ φ^n j(g).
* `New.Lift.Chart.S`, `New.Lift.Chart.bicommutant`: for a chart, the Λ-subalgebra S of A_inf that is
  the image of the chart's map Λ[[X]] → A_inf, with `k.coord₀ : A_inf → S` an S-linear retraction of
  A_inf onto S, and the subalgebra S_B of B^+, the closure of S[E/p] with p inverted.
* `New.Period.hodgeFil`: the step Fil^n = t^n B_dR^+ of the filtration of B_dR, for n in ℤ.

modules.title: The frame theorem for a period matrix, with Frobenius and Galois action on the frame
modules.group: Charts, period matrices and Kisin modules
modules.note:
The frame theorem `New.Lift.Chart.IsPeriodMatrix.exists_frame` for a period matrix `U`
(`New.Lift.Chart.IsPeriodMatrix`) over a chart with ring `S ⊂ A_inf`: the basis `Q`, `Z` of
`New.Lift.Chart.IsPeriodMatrix.exists_basis` is completed by partial inverses of `Q` and `Z`, a
Frobenius matrix `B` over `S`, and the Galois action on `Z`. The key point is `p ∤ det Q`; it rests
on

* `New.Lift.Chart.exists_det_ne_zero`: a nonzero determinant from a separating set of rows;
* `New.exists_mulVec_eq_zero_and_forall_comp_eq`: Artin's minimal support argument over a valuation
  ring, applied to the reduction of `Q` modulo `p` over the tilt `O^♭`.

Here `π` is `WittVector.constantCoeff`, the reduction `A_inf → O^♭` modulo `p`, `ainfToBPlus` is the
map `A_inf → B⁺`, and `(n, g)` in `New.Period.FrobGal` acts as `φ ^ n g`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.Chart.E`: The image in S of the series X^e A + p; it equals ξ times a unit of A_inf.
* `New.Lift.Chart.bicommutant`: The S-subalgebra S_B of those y in B⁺ whose multiplication commutes
  with every S-linear endomorphism of B⁺ that maps `New.Period.amaxImage` into itself.
* `New.Period.tau`: The element τ = [ε^{1/p}] − 1 of A_inf, where the brackets denote the
  Teichmüller lift.
* `New.Lift.Chart.S`: For a chart, the Λ-subalgebra S of A_inf that is the image of the chart's map
  Λ[[X]] → A_inf.
* `New.Lift.Chart`: A chart: a Λ-algebra map Λ[[X]] → A_inf, Λ = W(F_{p^f}), sending X to a non-unit
  Teichmüller lift z = [u] and a series X^e A + p, A a unit, to ξ times a unit.
modules.literature:
Known result: Kisin lattice (Breuil–Kisin module) of a crystalline lattice. Only existence is proved
here, of a frame over A_inf with a Frobenius matrix over S, which spans the crystalline periods up
to powers of E. Finite height is not stated, and there is no equivalence of categories. The proof
works directly by linear retractions onto the Breuil–Kisin ring, without slope theory or étale
φ-modules. Source: M. Kisin, Crystalline representations and F-crystals, Progr. Math. 253 (2006),
459–496; Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze, Integral p-adic Hodge theory, Publ. IHÉS 128 (2018), 4.26–4.34;
Cais–Liu, On F-crystalline representations, Doc. Math. 21 (2016).

modules.title: Kisin modules of Kummer charts: lattices with jump sets, letter projectors, invariant forms
modules.group: Charts, period matrices and Kisin modules
modules.note:
For a Kummer chart `k : New.Lift.KummerChart Γ` there is a ring S ⊂ A_inf, the image of Λ⟦X⟧ with
Λ = W(𝔽_{p^f}), and a subgroup Γ' of Γ. Kisin modules are defined inside `L.Ambient = W(C^♭) ⊗ L`
for a lattice L with prescribed jump sets. The objects are functorial in L and compatible with
Frobenius and with Γ'. They split according to the letters `i ∈ 𝔽_{p^f}ˣ`, on which the root of
unity ζ of the coefficients acts as the Teichmüller lift `ω i = letterTeich i`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.Letter`: the letters, the units i of 𝔽_{p^f}. For coefficients O with
  ζ^(p^f − 1) = 1 (`New.Lift.KummerChart.Coeffs`), the letter i cuts out the part
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.letterPart` where ζ = [i].
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice`: a lattice L, crystalline over Γ', with a finite set
  `jumpSet i` of integers for each letter that holds its jumps at the embeddings above i.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.forms`: forms, A_inf-linear maps to B_dR that are Γ'-equivariant
  on 1 ⊗ L.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinAinf`, `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinModule`,
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinLoc`: an A_inf-module cut out by forms, the Kisin module N,
  and N with all φ^a E inverted.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.mem_letterPart_iff_letterProj`,
  `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.sum_letterProj`: `e i = letterProj i` projects onto the letter
  `i`, and the `e i` sum to the identity.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.exists_span_formsOfType_mod_pred`: the functionals of type `u`
  at `i`, modulo those of type `u - 1`, are spanned over Q̄_p by at most `L.jumpMultiplicity i u` of
  them.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.formsOfType_subset_pred_of_notMem`: if `n ∉ L.jumpSet i`, the
  functionals of type `n` at `i` are of type `n - 1`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.KummerChart`: a chart Λ⟦X⟧ → A_inf (ring `S`, element `E` generating ker θ,
  `frobE a` = φ^a(E)) together with a subgroup Γ' of Γ whose fixed field it belongs to.
* `New.Lift.GalLattice`: a finite free O-module with an O-linear representation of Γ.
* `New.Period.WittCFlat`: the ring W(C^♭) of p-typical Witt vectors over the fraction field C^♭ of
  the tilt O^♭ of the ring of integers of C_p.
* `New.Period.overZp`: a representation of Γ on a module T over a Z_p-algebra R, regarded as a
  Z_p-linear representation.
* `New.Period.jump`: the multiplicity of a Hodge–Tate jump u of a representation at an embedding γ
  of the coefficients into ℂ_p.
modules.literature:
Known result: Hodge–Tate weights of Kisin modules. This is the analogue, for the Kisin module of one
Kummer chart inside A_inf, of the statements on Wach modules in the literature. This file proves
only the bounds on the weights, not that the Galois action is trivial modulo the variable. It holds
per unramified embedding of the coefficients, and it gives only upper bounds by the multiplicity of
each jump.
Source: L. Berger, Limites de représentations cristallines, Compositio Math. 140 (2004), 1473–1498,
§III; N. Wach, Représentations p-adiques potentiellement cristallines, Bull. SMF 124 (1996),
375–400.

See also `Lib.PadicHodge.Kisin.PeriodMatrixFrame`.

modules.title: The frame theorem for Kisin modules and stability under normalising Galois elements. Its head has an overview of the theory.
modules.group: Charts, period matrices and Kisin modules
modules.note:
Let `L` be a lattice datum over a Kummer chart `k`. The ring `S` of `k` has a variable `z` and the
element `E = z ^ e * unit + p`, and `k.frobE m` is `φ ^ m E`; `phiInvToBdR 0` is the map
`Ainf → BdR`. Let `h = L.jumpBound` and `τ = [ε^{1/p}] − 1`. A form is an `Ainf`-linear map
`W(C♭) ⊗ L → B_dR`. Those in `L.forms` are `Γ'`-equivariant on `1 ⊗ L`. They cut out the
`Ainf`-module `L.kisinAinf` and the Kisin module `N = L.kisinModule` over `S`. `L.ainfLattice` is
`Ainf ⊗ L`; `L.fracSpan` holds the `x` with `r • x ∈ L.ainfLattice` for some non-zero divisor `r` of
`Ainf`, and `L.frobKisinAinf l` is `φ ^ l (L.kisinAinf)`.

## Overview of this theory

A chart (`New.Lift.Chart`) is a `Λ`-algebra map `Λ⟦X⟧ → A_inf`, with `Λ = W(𝔽_{p^f})`. It sends `X`
to a non-unit Teichmüller lift `z = [ϖ^♭]`. It sends some `X^e V + p`, with `V` a unit, to a
generator `E` of `ker θ`. `S` is its image. `B⁺` (`New.Period.BPlus`) receives `A_inf` and maps to
`B_max` (`New.Period.Bmax`) and `B_dR`. Its `S`-subalgebra `S_B` (`New.Lift.Chart.bicommutant`) is
the `p`-adic closure of `S[E/p]` with `p` inverted
(`New.Lift.Chart.adjoinEDivPClosure_eq_bicommutant`). Put `μ = [ε] - 1`, with `ε` a compatible
system of `p`-power roots of unity, and `τ = φ⁻¹ μ`.

* Let `K` be the field fixed by an open subgroup `G_K` of `Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p)`. There is a Kummer chart
  (`New.Lift.KummerChart`) with `Λ` and `θ z` fixed by `G_K` and `e f = [K : ℚ_p]`
  (`New.Lift.exists_kummerChart`).
* Let `c` be a chart for `G_K` (`IsChartOf`). Let `T` be a crystalline `ℤ_p`-lattice with action
  `ρ`, whose jumps (the `k` with `New.Period.jump` nonzero) lie in `[-a, b]`. In a basis of `T`
  there are three objects. The first is `P`, invertible over `B_max`, with `ρ(g) · g P = P`. The
  second is a unit `v` with `E τ v = μ`. The third is `U` over `B⁺`, whose image in `B_max` is
  `(E τ)^a P`. This `U` satisfies the predicate `IsPeriodMatrix` with height `a + b` and Frobenius
  factor `v^a` (`New.Lift.Chart.IsChartOf.exists_isPeriodMatrixOf`).
* Take such a `U` of height `h` and factor `v`. There are `Q` and `Q'` over `A_inf`, `Z` over `S_B`
  and `B` over `S` with `Q Q' = τ^h`, `U Z = E^h Q` and `φ Q = v Q B`
  (`New.Lift.Chart.IsPeriodMatrix.exists_frame`).
* On a Kummer chart, let `h = jumpBound`. Let `N` be the `S`-module `kisinModule` and `M` its
  `A_inf`-span `kisinAinf`. Then `τ^h` maps `M` into `ainfLattice` and back, and `E^h φ N ⊆ N`. Take
  a crystalline form `λ` (`crysForms`, valued in `B_dR`). Then `E^h λ(N)` lies in the image of
  `S_B`. Suppose `d ∈ A_inf` is such that `d ∣ E^m r` in `B⁺` forces `d ∣ r`. Then `x ∈ M` lies in
  `d M` once, for one `n`, `E^n λ(x) ∈ d B⁺` for all such `λ`
  (`New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.mem_smul_kisinAinf_of_crysForms`).

This is a substitute, in the form needed here, for part of Kisin's theorem on the module of a
crystalline lattice (Kisin 2006; Bhatt–Morrow–Scholze 2018). The inclusion `E^n N ⊆ S φ N` and an
equivalence of categories are not stated.

Contents of the files. `Charts`: coordinates and an approximation lemma.
`Bicommutant`: extension to `B⁺`.
`PeriodMatrixBasis`: `U`, and `Q` with `det Q ≠ 0`. `PeriodMatrixFrame`: `p ∤ det Q`, hence the
frame. `KummerChartDeRham`: the different, and values in `B_dR`. `Modules`: `M`, `N` and the
`B_dR`-valued forms. `FrameTheorem`: `N` as the `S`-span of the columns of `τ^{-h} Q`, using
`Lib.PadicHodge.RadiusLemma`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.frame_theorem`: a relation `∑ c i • v i = 0` among vectors of
  `L.valueFieldPoints L.fracSpan` still holds after applying any `k.S`-linear `f : Ainf → k.S` to
  the coefficients (`New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.FrameProperties`).
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.valueFieldPoints_frobKisinAinf_eq_span`: the vectors of
  `φ ^ l (L.kisinAinf)` on which all forms in `L.forms` take values in `k.valueField 0` form the
  `S`-span of `φ ^ l N`.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.smul_mem_kisinAinf`: an element `g` that conjugates `Γ'` into
  itself preserves the module `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinAinf`. The reason is that
  conjugation by `g` keeps forms `Γ'`-equivariant
  (`New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.conjForm_mem_forms`).

Notions from other files:
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice`: A finite free O-module with an action of Γ, crystalline over
  Γ', together with a finite set of integers for each embedding of O in `ℂ_[p]` that contains the
  jumps at that embedding. It also carries finite sets of integers indexed by `Letter`, which this
  file does not use directly.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.Ambient`: The module W(C^♭)⊗L for the lattice underlying L;
  `DiagTensor.mk 1 t` is the vector 1 ⊗ t.
* `New.Lift.KummerChart.JumpLattice.kisinAinf`: The x in A_inf[1/τ] ⊗ L with μ(φ^n x) in B_dR^+ for
  all n ≥ 1 and all μ in `L.forms`, where τ = [ε^{1/p}] − 1. The Kisin module consists of those x on
  which all forms in `L.forms` take values in the subfield `k.valueField 0` of B_dR.

modules.title: Uniform period bounds and limits of crystalline lattices with bounded jumps
modules.group: Limits of crystalline and Galois representations
modules.note:
Let `A = New.Period.Amax` and `B = New.Period.Bmax`, with tensor products over `ℤ_p`. A continuous,
trace-nondegenerate `p`-adic limit of continuous crystalline representations with jumps in `[0, h]`
is crystalline. The limit is formulated through representations of the group ring `ℤ_p[G]`,
restricted along a multiplicative map from a local Galois group.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.IsCrystallineUpTo`: crystalline with all Hodge–Tate jumps (`New.Period.jump`) in [0,
  h].
* `New.Period.PadicRep`: a matrix representation of Γ over Q̄_p, bundled with its index set.
* `New.Lift.uniform_period_bound`: one element `a` of the period ring `A = New.Period.Amax` bounds
  the denominators of the periods of all crystalline `ℤ_p`-lattices with Hodge–Tate jumps in
  `[0, h]` (`New.Period.IsCrystallineUpTo`). The element `a` is chosen for the given `Γ`, with its
  `OverGp Γ p` instance (the map `toGp` to `G_p`), and for the given `h`.
* `New.Period.exists_finite_groupRing_quotient`: the image of `ℤ_p[G]` in finitely many continuous
  representations is a finite free `ℤ_p`-algebra with the properties
  `New.Period.IsFiniteGroupRingQuotient`.
* `New.Period.isCrystalline_of_trace_limit`: the limit theorem.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.IsCrystalline`: T is crystalline: the elements of B⊗T fixed by all of Γ span B⊗T over
  B.
* `New.Period.Amax`: Colmez's period ring A_max, the p-adic completion of A_inf[X]/(pX − ξ).
* `New.Period.Bmax`: The period ring B = B^+[1/μ] (Colmez's B_max, used in place of Fontaine's
  B_cris), over which crystalline representations are defined; B^+ = A[1/p] is `New.Period.BPlus`.
* `New.IsTraceNondeg`: for a representation r, any x in the span of r(G) with tr(x r(g)) = 0 for all
  g is zero.
* `OverGp Γ p`: a group Γ with a homomorphism `toGp` to G_p = Gal(Q̄_p/Q_p) whose image is open.
* `New.Period.fixedPeriods ρ B F`: the elements of B ⊗ T fixed by `toGp g ⊗ ρ g` for F-almost all g.
* `New.Lift.Chart` c with `c.IsChartOf j`: a chart W(F_q)⟦X⟧ → A_inf with coefficients `WittFq c.f`,
  sending X to z; `IsChartOf j` says that every g in G_p that fixes `WittFq c.f` pointwise and fixes
  θ(z) lies in j(Γ).
* `New.Lift.AdicBasis I A`: for an ideal I of a ring Λ and a Λ-module A, a topological basis of A
  for the I-adic topology, with coordinate forms.

modules.title: Hodge–Tate jumps with bounded denominators and local conditions at limits of traces. Its head has an overview of the theory.
modules.group: Limits of crystalline and Galois representations
modules.note:
The multiplicities of Hodge–Tate jumps can be read from traces with uniformly bounded denominators,
which lets jumps pass to `p`-adic limits of representations. These bounded denominators are used to
prove `New.GaloisRep.local_clauses_of_trace_limit`.

## Overview of this theory

One period ring `B = New.Period.Bmax` defines crystalline and potentially crystalline
representations `T` of a group `Γ` mapping to `G_p = Gal(ℚ̄_p/ℚ_p)`, such as `G_K` with `K/ℚ_p`
finite. This ring is Colmez's `B_max`, not Fontaine's `B_cris`, and their comparison is not
formalised. `B` also gives a linear Frobenius and the crystalline cocycles `Z_f(T)`. The Hodge–Tate
jumps of `T` form a multiset of integers, defined via `ℂ_p ⊗ T`.

* `New.Period.ax_mem_closure_fixedField`, `New.Period.tate_eq_zero_of_cyclotomicGp_twist`: for a
  subgroup `J` of `G_p`, `ℂ_p^J` lies in the closure of `ℚ̄_p^J`. An element of `ℂ_p(i)`, `i ≠ 0`,
  fixed by an open subgroup is `0`.
* `New.Period.IsAdmissible.of_jointly_injective`: being crystalline, or potentially crystalline,
  passes to subrepresentations of finite direct sums.
* `New.Period.crysCocycles.finrank_eq`: let `T` be a potentially crystalline `ℤ_p`-lattice with
  jumps `J`. Then `Z_f(T)` is finitely generated of rank `rk T + n · #(negative jumps)`, where `n`
  is the index of the image of `Γ` in `G_p`.
* `New.GaloisRep.local_clauses_of_trace_limit`: let `r` be a continuous Galois representation with
  non-degenerate trace form. Let its trace be a uniform limit of linear combinations of traces of
  continuous representations unramified or crystalline at a place `A`. Require finitely many
  approximations, or the same jumps for all terms. Then `r` is unramified or crystalline at `A`. Its
  jumps follow if their multiplicities are compatible with the limit. A polynomial killing an
  element `s` at `A` passes to `r`, given bounded degrees and convergence weighted by each
  coefficient.

The development proves only the parts of the standard theory that it uses: of the Ax–Sen–Tate
theorem only Ax's weaker form, and of Tate's theorem only the statement on `H⁰`. The notions below
take the place of Fontaine's admissible representations, of the Weil–Deligne representation and of
the Bloch–Kato rank formula. For local–global compatibility of automorphic Galois representations,
only the passage to limits is proved, with `r` given. Crystalline means that the invariants span
`B ⊗ T`.

In place of the Weil–Deligne representation stands `New.Period.linearFrob`. For `s ∈ Γ` and `m ∈ ℕ`,
it is a chosen `B`-linear endomorphism of `B ⊗ T`. It agrees with `φ^m s ⊗ s` on `D_pcris(T)` when
one exists, where `φ` is the Frobenius of `B`. In place of `H¹_f` stands the rank of `Z_f(T)`.

Organisation of `Lib.PadicHodge`. (1) `PeriodRings`: Ax's theorem, `A_inf`, Fontaine's map `θ`,
`B`, the period `t` of `ℤ_p(1)`, `B_dR`. (2) `TateSen`: Tate's theorem, invariants of `B_dR`.
(3) `Crystalline`: `Basic` (definitions, twists), `HodgeTateJumps`, `Regularity` (regularity of
`B`, using `Kisin`). (4) `BlochKato`: the rank, by the fundamental exact sequence; duality is in
`Lib.ClassField.LocalDuality.CrystallineDuality`. (5) `Limit`: the trace-limit theorem.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.exists_uniform_trace_sum_eq_jump`: the multiplicity of one jump is `t` times a sum of
  traces with coefficients of norm at most `1`, where `t` is the same for every crystalline lattice
  with jumps in `[0, n]` and depends only on `Γ`, `n` and the jump.

Notions from other files:
* `New.GaloisRep.HasJumpsAt`: For each local datum at `A` with embedding `e` and each `g` in
  `Gal(ℚ̄_ℓ/ℚ_ℓ)`, the Hodge–Tate jumps of `r` at `g`, with multiplicity, are `J` at the embedding
  `ι_ℓ⁻¹ ∘ g⁻¹ ∘ e` of `E` in `ℂ`.
* `New.Period.IsKilledBy`: the form of `PolyKillsAt` above ℓ. For a Weil pair (s, k), with s acting
  on residues as x ↦ x^(1/ℓ^k), it says that the representation T is potentially crystalline. It
  also says that P kills the operator β = `linearFrob` on `Bmax ℓ` ⊗ T, which acts as φ^k s on the
  elements fixed by all g near 1.
* `New.Period.IsPotentiallyCrystalline`: the elements of B⊗T fixed by all g with j(g) near 1 span
  B⊗T over B.
modules.literature:
Known result: Limits of crystalline representations with bounded weights are crystalline. Here the
hypothesis is a uniform limit of traces with unbounded coefficients and ranks, and crystallinity is
Liu's theorem applied to the image of the group ring. The file also proves limit formulas for the
multiplicities of jumps and for killing polynomials. Source: T. Liu, Torsion p-adic Galois
representations and a conjecture of Fontaine, Ann. Sci. ENS 40 (2007) 633–674; L. Berger, Limites de
représentations cristallines, Compositio Math. 140 (2004) 1473–1498; for the passage from traces to
the image of the group ring, P. Wake, C. Wang-Erickson, Deformation conditions for
pseudorepresentations, Forum Math. Sigma 7 (2019).

modules.title: Tilting, Fontaine's θ, the ring O_C and Ax's theorem on Galois invariants in ℂ_p
modules.group: Fontaine's period rings A_inf, A, B and B_dR
modules.note:
This file studies the absolute Galois group `New.Gp` of `ℚ_p`, its action on `ℂ_p`, and its
invariants. For `p`-adically complete rings in which `p` is not a unit, the untilt and Fontaine's
`θ` are natural, and they are onto if the ring is also absolutely integrally closed. Ax's theorem
then describes the elements of `ℂ_p` fixed by a subgroup `J` of `New.Gp` as limits of algebraic
elements fixed by `J`.

## Main definitions and results

* Tilting for a ring `R` in which `p` is not a unit. `New.Variety.tiltMap` makes Mathlib's
  `PreTilt R p` functorial. For `p`-adically complete `R`, the untilt `x ↦ x^♯` and Fontaine's `θ`
  are natural in `R` (`New.Variety.untilt_tiltMap`, `New.Variety.fontaineTheta_map_tiltMap`). Both
  are onto if `R` is absolutely integrally closed
  (`New.Variety.fontaineTheta_surjective_of_isAbsIntegrallyClosed`). The tilt of a `p`-adically
  complete valuation ring is a valuation ring.
* The Galois group `New.Gp` of `ℚ̄_p / ℚ_p` and its cyclotomic character `New.cyclotomicGp`.
* The continuous isometric action of `New.Gp` on `ℂ_p` (`New.completionAction`), which restricts
  to an action by ring automorphisms on the ring of integers `New.OC`.
* `O_C` is `p`-adically complete and absolutely integrally closed, with `O_C[1/p] = ℂ_p`.
* `New.Period.ax_mem_closure_fixedField`: Ax's theorem; an element fixed by a subgroup `J` is a
  limit of algebraic elements fixed by `J`.
* `New.Period.exists_algebraic_of_fixed_near_one`: an element fixed by a neighbourhood of `1` is
  algebraic.

Notions from other files:
* `New.cyclotomicChar`: the ℓ-adic cyclotomic character Γ → ℤ_ℓ^× of a group Γ that acts on a
  field Ω by ring automorphisms; `New.cyclotomicGp` is the case Γ = `New.Gp p`, Ω = ℚ̄_p, ℓ = p.

modules.title: The ring A_inf, the elements ε, μ, τ, ξ, the kernel of θ and adic completeness
modules.group: Fontaine's period rings A_inf, A, B and B_dR
modules.note:
`G_p` is the absolute Galois group of `ℚ_p`, and `O_C` is the ring of integers of `ℂ_p`. Fontaine's
ring `A_inf = W(O^♭)` is built from the tilt `O^♭` of `O_C`, together with Fontaine's map
`θ : A_inf → O_C`, the Frobenius `φ`, and an action of `ℕ × G_p`.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.OFlat`, `New.Period.CFlat`: the tilt O^♭ of O_C and its fraction field;
  `New.Period.Ainf`, `New.Period.WittCFlat`: their rings of Witt vectors; `New.Period.theta`:
  Fontaine's θ : A_inf → O_C.
* `New.Period.epsPow`: a homomorphism s ↦ ε^s from ℚ to O^♭ that untilts to primitive roots of
  unity; `New.Period.tau` = [ε^(1/p)] − 1, `New.Period.mu` = [ε] − 1, `New.Period.xi` with ξ τ = μ.
* `New.Period.FrobGal` = ℕ × G_p acts on O^♭ and A_inf, (n, g) as φⁿ g. Groups acting on O^♭ also
  act on C^♭ and W(C^♭). `New.Period.frobEnd` is φ.
* `New.Period.theta_eq_zero_iff_xi_dvd`: the kernel of `θ` is generated by `ξ`.
* `New.Period.mu_dvd_of_theta_frobEnd`: `μ` divides every element killed by all `θ φ ^ j`.
  `New.Period.tau_dvd_of_theta_frobEnd` gives the same for `τ` when only `j ≥ 1` is assumed.
* `New.Period.Ainf.isAdicComplete_span_pair`: `A_inf` is adically complete for the ideal of any two
  non-units.

Notions from other files:
* `New.actionOfHoms`: The action of a monoid M on a ring B by ring endomorphisms given by a family
  f(m) with f(1) the identity and f(ab) = f(a)∘f(b).
* `New.Variety.tiltMap`: For a ring homomorphism f: R → R', the induced ring homomorphism between
  the inverse limits of R/p and R'/p along x ↦ x^p.
* `New.shiftDiff`: For π in R, the operator (x_j) ↦ (x_j − π x_{j+1}) on sequences in an R-module.
* `New.Variety.IsAbsIntegrallyClosed`: A ring is absolutely integrally closed if every monic
  polynomial of positive degree over it has a root.
* `PreTilt.untilt`: The multiplicative map x ↦ x^♯ from the tilt of a ring R to R.
* `New.ThePrime p`: The class saying that the natural number p is prime.

modules.title: The period rings A, B⁺, B and B_dR⁺: θ, Frobenius, domains and contraction
modules.group: Fontaine's period rings A_inf, A, B and B_dR
modules.note:
`New.Period.Ainf` is `A_inf`, for the prime `p` supplied by the class `ThePrime p`. In it, `ξ`
(`New.Period.xi`) generates the kernel of Fontaine's `θ`, `μ = [ε] - 1 = ξ τ` with
`τ = [ε^(1/p)] - 1`, where `ε ∈ O^♭` is a compatible system `(1, ζ_p, ζ_{p²}, …)` of `p`-power roots
of unity and `[·]` is the Teichmüller lift, and `φ` is the Frobenius. The map `θ` is defined on `A`,
`B⁺` and `B_dR⁺` (`New.Period.thetaBdR`). The file studies `A` modulo `p` and its divisibility by
powers of `p`. It shows that `θ` has kernel `ξ B⁺` on `B⁺` and that `B_dR⁺` is a discrete valuation
ring. It deduces that `A`, `B⁺` and `B` are domains.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Period.Amax`: `A`, the `p`-adic completion of `A_inf[X] / (p X - ξ)`, with the existence half
  of its universal property, `New.Period.Amax.exists_lift`.
* `New.Period.BPlus`: `B⁺ = A[1/p]`; `New.Period.Bmax`: `B = B⁺[1/μ]`; `New.Period.BdRPlus`: the
  `ξ`-adic completion `B_dR⁺` of `B⁺`.
* `New.Period.actBmax`: the monoid `New.Period.FrobGal = ℕ × G_p`, with `G_p` the absolute Galois
  group of `ℚ_p`, in which `(n, g)` stands for `φ^n g`, acts on `A`, `B⁺` and `B`. On `B` this needs
  `New.Period.isUnit_smul_of_dvd_mu`, which rests on `New.Period.associated_p_frobEnd_xi`: `φ ξ` is
  `p` times a unit.
* `New.Period.thetaBPlus`: `θ` extends to `A`, with `X ↦ 0`, and to a map from `B⁺` onto `ℂ_[p]`
  (`New.Period.thetaBPlus_surjective`).
* `New.Period.BdRPlus.prime_xi`: `ξ` is prime in `B_dR⁺`, so `B_dR⁺` is a discrete valuation ring
  with uniformiser `ξ`.
* `New.Period.exists_Ainf_eq_of_contraction`: let `V ⊆ B⁺` (`New.Period.BPlus`) lie in the image
  `New.Period.amaxImage` of the period ring `A`, and let every `v ∈ V` satisfy `ξ ^ n v = u φ(w)`
  for some `w ∈ V`, with `u ∈ A_inf` fixed and `φ` the Frobenius. Then `p ^ (n + 1) V` lies in the
  image of `A_inf`: each application of `φ` improves an approximation by `A_inf` by one power of
  `p`.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.Ainf`: the ring `A_inf` of `p`-typical Witt vectors over the tilt `O^♭` of the ring of
  integers of `ℂ_p`.
* `New.Period.xi`: the element `ξ = ∑_{i < p} [ε^{1/p}]^i` of `A_inf`, so that `ξ τ = μ`.
* `New.Period.theta`: Fontaine's ring homomorphism `θ` from `A_inf` onto the ring `New.OC p` of
  integers of `ℂ_p`, sending the Teichmüller lift `[x]` to `x^♯`.

modules.title: The cyclotomic action on μ, the period t, and the de Rham field B_dR
modules.group: Fontaine's period rings A_inf, A, B and B_dR
modules.note:
This file studies the Galois and Frobenius actions on Fontaine's period rings for `ℂ_[p]`. We write
A_inf = `New.Period.Ainf` (Witt vectors of `OFlat`, the tilt of the integers of `ℂ_[p]`),
ε = `New.Period.epsTilt` (a compatible system of `p`-power roots of unity in the tilt), μ = [ε] − 1,
ξ for the generator of the kernel of θ, φ for Frobenius (`New.Period.frobEnd`) and χ for the
cyclotomic character `New.cyclotomicGp`. Let B_dR⁺ = `New.Period.BdRPlus`, the ξ-adic completion of
B⁺ = `New.Period.BPlus`. The fraction field B_dR of B_dR⁺ contains B = B⁺[1/μ] and Q̄_p
equivariantly.

## Main definitions and results

* `New.Lift.mu_sq_dvd_smul_mu_sub`: in `New.Period.Ainf`, the Witt vectors of the tilt of the
  integers of `ℂ_[p]`, an element `g` of the Galois group `New.Gp p` sends `μ = [ε] - 1` to `χ(g) μ`
  modulo `μ ^ 2`. Here `ε` is `New.Period.epsTilt` and `χ` is the cyclotomic character. The
  divisibility `μ ^ 2 ∣ g μ - χ(g) μ` holds in `A_inf` itself; the proof checks it modulo every
  power of the ideal `(p, ξ)`, where `ξ` generates the kernel of Fontaine's map `θ`.
* `New.Period.exists_tPeriod`: some unit multiple `t` of `p μ` has `φ t = p t` and `g t = χ(g) t`.
* `New.Period.BdR`: the fraction field of B_dR⁺; G_p acts on it and B embeds in it equivariantly.
* An embedding of Q̄_p in B_dR⁺, got by lifting along θ since Q̄_p is formally étale over ℚ_p;
  `New.Period.thetaBdR_algebraMap_padicAlgCl` says it is a section of θ,
  `New.Period.BdR.smul_algebraMap_padicAlgCl` that it is G_p-equivariant.
* `New.Period.Bmax.fundamental_sequence_surjective`: (φ − 1, inclusion) maps B onto
  B × B_dR / B_dR⁺, the surjectivity in the fundamental exact sequence.

Notions from other files:
* `New.Period.Amax`: The ring A, the p-adic completion of A_inf[ξ/p]; B⁺ = A[1/p].
* `New.Period.mu`, `New.Period.tau`, `New.Period.xi`: The elements μ = [ε] − 1, τ = [ε^{1/p}] − 1
  and ξ = Σ_{0 ≤ i < p} [ε^{1/p}]^i of A_inf; ξτ = μ and φ(τ) = μ.
modules.literature:
Known result: Fontaine's period rings and the fundamental exact sequence. Here Colmez's B_max
replaces B_cris and the period t is built without logarithms. The part of Fontaine's regularity that
is used, namely that the invariants of the fraction field of B already lie in B, is proved in
`Lib.PadicHodge.Crystalline.Regularity` (`New.Period.fontaine_regularity`). Source: P. Colmez,
Théorie d'Iwasawa des représentations de de Rham d'un corps local, Ann. of Math. 148 (1998),
III.2-III.3; J.-M. Fontaine, Le corps des périodes p-adiques, Astérisque 223 (1994); X. Caruso, An
introduction to p-adic period rings (2019), §3.
